description: deixis mandatory Node[T] navigation vectors — own, at and valueAt of ADR 0010 §4 and PATH.md. own is total, so its result is the payload itself. at and valueAt are partial: their result is {"defined": …} or {"undefined": {}}, with no reason spelled. {"defined": null} (json slot) and {"undefined": {}} are therefore different results. Paths are arrays of hex keys; [] is ε. Every case declares its slot, as defined in vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md. Hand-authored from docs/design/0010-mandatory-node-values.md, docs/TREE.md and docs/PATH.md as merged in 1a9bb6d, and from nothing else. No implementation of the mandatory API existed when these were written. Items X1, X4, X18 and X19; each note names the defect (W) it catches. 24 cases.

cases.name: m-nav-own-root
cases.note: X1. own(Node(t,m)) = t (ADR 0010 §4): the payload itself, not a wrapper around it. Catches W1.

cases.name: m-nav-valueat-epsilon-is-root-value
cases.note: X1. valueAt(n,ε) = own(at(n,ε)) = own(n).

cases.name: m-nav-valueat-interior
cases.note: X1. The node at [6b] has a child and its own value; PATH says interior paths carry T. Catches W1 and any reading of values as terminal-only.

cases.name: m-nav-valueat-terminal
cases.note: X1. Resolution follows the keys in order: at(at(n,[6b]),[6a]).

cases.name: m-nav-at-epsilon-is-self
cases.note: X1. at(n,ε) ≡ n (ADR 0010 §4; PATH: a node points at itself with no keys spent).

cases.name: m-nav-at-interior-returns-whole-subtree
cases.note: X1. The subtree at [6b] is returned whole: its own value and its child.

cases.name: m-nav-valueat-missing-child
cases.note: X4. [62] is not in D_n. Missing paths refuse; no default value or node is created (ADR 0010 §4).

cases.name: m-nav-at-below-a-terminal-node
cases.note: X4. The node at [61] is childless, so it resolves no nonempty path, whatever its own value (PATH, resolution).

cases.name: m-nav-at-missing-below-interior-does-not-create
cases.note: X4. PATH, 'What resolution is not': a miss does not bring a node into being.

cases.name: m-nav-json-valueat-null-leaf
cases.note: X4. A legal null payload at an existing path is defined, with value null (PATH valueAt: if T includes null, it is a legal payload at an existing path). Catches W3.

cases.name: m-nav-json-at-null-leaf
cases.note: X4. The node carrying null exists and is returned. It is Node(null,∅), not a miss.

cases.name: m-nav-json-valueat-missing-sibling-of-null
cases.note: X4. The pair to m-nav-json-valueat-null-leaf: the same tree, a path that does not exist. The two results must differ.

cases.name: m-nav-json-valueat-null-interior
cases.note: X4. An interior node whose value is null. Catches W3.

cases.name: m-nav-json-navigate-through-null-interior
cases.note: X4. Resolution walks through a node whose payload is null; the payload does not stop navigation. An implementation that reads null as a missing node cannot reach [62,63]. Catches W3.

cases.name: m-nav-option-valueat-root-none
cases.note: X4. Under the option slot, none is a legal payload: valueAt returns it as defined. It is not a missing node (TREE: none does not denote a missing node). Catches W1 and W3.

cases.name: m-nav-option-valueat-none-child
cases.note: X4. A childless node carrying none exists.

cases.name: m-nav-option-valueat-some-is-the-payload
cases.note: X1. The payload at [62] is the option value some(v) itself. The core does not unwrap it; T is Option[fixture] here (ADR 0010 §1). Catches an implementation that strips the option.

cases.name: m-nav-option-valueat-missing
cases.note: X4. The navigation failure is represented independently of every legal payload, none included (ADR 0010 §4).

cases.name: m-nav-unit-valueat-leaf
cases.note: X4. Under Node[Unit], every existing node carries the unit.

cases.name: m-nav-unit-valueat-missing
cases.note: X4. The pair to m-nav-unit-valueat-leaf: under Node[Unit] every value is equal, so only definedness separates existing from missing.

cases.name: m-nav-json-payload-spelling-a-node-is-not-entered
cases.note: X18. The root's payload is a JSON object that happens to spell a node with a child at [61]. It is opaque content: resolution walks children only and never enters a value (PATH). The root is childless.

cases.name: m-nav-json-payload-spelling-a-node-returned-whole
cases.note: X18. The same node: its value is that object, returned as is.

cases.name: m-nav-empty-key-path
cases.note: X19. [""] is the path of one empty key and reaches the child; ε would give the root's a. The empty key is a key.

cases.name: m-nav-non-utf8-key-exact
cases.note: X19. The only child key is ff00. The byte string ff is a different key, not a prefix match. Keys are exact bytes and need not be UTF-8.
